correctness.rationale: The normalized duality formula is explicit; compactness of T and T' on reflexive ℓp and ℓp' forces Te_n,T'e_n'→0. The normalized disjoint-support vector au+be_n has exact J decomposition. The limiting defect estimate δ≥a||Tu||−a^(p−1)||T|| is uniform over compact maps, maximizing at a=(p−1)^−1/(p−2). For the coordinate rank-one projection, δ exactly equals max_{t∈[0,1]}(t−t^(p−1)), proving universal optimality; endpoint asymptotics follow directly. No finite experiment is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 program studies compact operators satisfying nonlinear duality self-adjointness; older exact-solution classification eliminates nonzero compact examples on non-Hilbert ℓp. The new theorem replaces that binary obstruction with the exact, attained quantitative separation for every compact operator, and finds a sharp p-dependent transition coefficient. This is a natural operator-ideal extremal invariant across a continuous family of exponents, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
